title: Client conformance: every response matches Jellyfin 12.4's API schema, and every route clients call answers
description: Findroid has stopped on the dogfood four times, each on a missing route or a field its strict SDK requires (#44, #47, #91, #94, #95), while jellyfin-web, which ignores what it doesn't read, played on. Check every response against Jellyfin 12.4's own OpenAPI schema, taken from the Jellyfin container the differential tier already starts, in the differential and e2e tiers; and check that every route the SDK clients call on their main paths answers. Where an SDK can run (the Kotlin SDK, as in ~/.cache/jellyscale/sdkjvm/Decode.java; @jellyfin/sdk), decode our answers with it too.
acceptanceCriteria: The differential tier checks every JSON response jellyscale gives it (each request of test/differential/requests.yaml and the tier's own sign-in and setup calls, stub routes included) against the type Jellyfin 12.4's OpenAPI schema gives that route and status, and fails on any violation

The e2e tier does the same for every JSON response jellyfin-web receives from jellyscale in each of its four gates (browse, play, subtitles, transcode), using the checked-in schema and no Jellyfin container

A violation is: a field the schema requires (however the 12.4 document marks it) that is absent or null, at any depth and in every element of an array, not only the first; a value of another type than the schema's (a string for a number, a fraction for an integer, null where not nullable, a string outside its enum, a malformed uuid or date-time); or no JSON body where the schema gives one. A field the schema does not list is not a violation

Shown by putting each of these back alone: each of #47's four sign-in fields on POST /Users/AuthenticateByName (SessionInfo.LastPlaybackCheckIn, SessionInfo.PlayState.PlaybackOrder, User.Policy.AuthenticationProviderId, User.Policy.PasswordResetProviderId); #94's source and stream fields on GET /Items/{itemId}; #95's stream fields on the second and later streams of a PlaybackInfo sent with a transcoding profile. Each fails the differential tier and every e2e gate that receives that response, and the failure names the request or route, the JSON path and the field

With ProductName put back to "jellyscale" (#44) the differential tier fails; it is a wrong value, which no schema catches, so the failure comes from SDK discovery or from comparing GET /System/Info/Public with Jellyfin's answer
No entry in compat/differences.yaml excuses a schema violation: with a #47 field removed and its difference listed there as a gap, the differential tier still fails
The same check run on Jellyfin 12.4's own answers to the differential requests reports no violation, so jellyscale is held to no rule Jellyfin's own answers break

A response is matched to its operation whatever the case of its path and the names of its parameters, and an alias is checked as the route it stands for; a JSON response that matches no operation or no declared type fails the tier unless its route is in a checked-in list with a reason
Each run says how many JSON responses it checked and on how many routes; a differential run or an e2e gate that checked none fails

A checked-in script produces the checked-in schema from the OpenAPI document of the jellyfin/jellyfin:12.4 image the differential tier starts, and the file records the image and server version it came from (12.4.0, the baseline of compat/endpoints.yaml)
The differential tier fails when the checked-in schema differs from what the script produces from the container it has started, so a hand edit or a stale copy fails

A checked-in list names, for each of Findroid, Android TV, Swiftfin and Streamyfin and each of startup, sign-in, home, browse, detail, playback, progress and stop, every request the client sends (method, route, query names as the client's SDK spells them, body, Authorization header form), with the client version or commit and whether it was read from source or seen in traffic; none of the 32 client-and-path cells is empty

The list holds the Findroid requests seen on the dogfood (#91, #94, #95): GET /System/Info/Public, /Users/Public, /Branding/Configuration and /QuickConnect/Enabled, POST /Users/AuthenticateByName, GET /Items/Suggestions?mediaType=Video&type=Movie&type=Series&limit=6, GET /Items/{itemId} and POST /Items/{itemId}/PlaybackInfo

In a tier CI already requires, each listed request is sent to a running jellyscale with a scanned library and a signed-in user and must answer 2xx, never 404, and a JSON answer must pass the schema check; shown by removing /Items/Suggestions (#91), which fails naming Findroid, home and the route

A listed request may go unanswered only where its row in compat/coverage-12.4.tsv is out-of-scope and its evidence names the client and path that call it; a row that is needed but not yet served is not a decision and fails, and go test ./compat still passes

In the differential or e2e tier in CI, jellyfin-sdk-kotlin 1.9.4's own serializers with ApiSerializer's settings (jars from Maven Central at pinned versions) decode answers taken from the running jellyscale, never stored samples: the sign-in result, GET /Sessions with an idle session and one playing a transcode, GET /Items/{itemId} for a film with several audio and subtitle streams, an episode and a series, an item listing, and PlaybackInfo for an H.264 and an HEVC film both as direct play and with a transcoding profile

The tier fails when the decoder rejects an answer, naming the model, the JSON path and the field; shown with a #95 field removed from the second stream of a transcode Play

source: escaped defects from the dogfood, Findroid, 2026-11-08 (#44, #47)
notes: jellyfin-web ignores fields it doesn't read, so it can't catch this class; Kotlin and Swift SDK clients decode strictly. Scheduled after the web-client work (user, 2026-11-08: focus on the web client first, then pivot to other clients). Findroid's first home-screen call, GET /Items/Suggestions, 404s; a parked implementation is on branch feat/items-suggestions. Moved up and widened 2026-11-11 (owner: the SDK is the primary way clients are built, other than the web client; evaluate what is required): it now also lists the routes each SDK client calls, since a missing route stops a client as surely as a missing field. /Items/Suggestions shipped in #91; the parked branch feat/items-suggestions is superseded. Rewritten 2026-11-12 from the architecture review: the API schema is a better oracle than scraping each SDK. Built 2026-11-13: compat/schema-12.4.json from the jellyfin/jellyfin:12.4 OpenAPI document (compat/gen-schema.sh); compat/conform checks every response in the differential and e2e tiers; compat/clients.yaml lists every request Findroid, Android TV, Swiftfin and Streamyfin send on their main paths, sent by the differential runner; the Kotlin SDK's decoder and @jellyfin/sdk's discovery run in CI. GET /MediaSegments/{itemId} answers an empty list until JS-052 (lead fix after Verify). Two lead corrections (PublicSystemInfo fields are nullable; four bugs in the e2e acceptance script).
